title: Forbidden City Tickets 2026 | China Travel Expert
description:
Everything you need to book and visit the Forbidden City (Palace Museum) in Beijing in 2026 — tickets, prices, the one-way route, and what not to miss inside.

The short answer: tickets are online only, released 7 days ahead and tied to your passport (no same-day sales), and the museum is closed on Mondays except public holidays. Standard admission is ¥60 through 31 October and ¥40 from 1 November, with the Treasure Gallery and Clock Gallery each ¥10 extra.

• Forbidden City admission ¥60 (1 Apr–31 Oct) / ¥40 (1 Nov–31 Mar), Treasure & Clock galleries +¥10 each; online-only, 7-day advance, passport-linked, closed Mondays except holidays — realchinatrip.com 'Forbidden City Beijing Tickets 2026' + sg.trip.com 'Forbidden City Tickets'.
• Palace of Versailles Passport €35 high season (1 Apr–31 Oct) / €25 low season, non-EEA adult — chateauversailles.fr '2026 ticketing' (official) + artvisitguide.com 'Versailles Tickets 2026'.
• One-way south-to-north route since 2 July 2011 (in at the Meridian Gate; out at the Gate of Divine Prowess or East Prosperity Gate); Hall of Supreme Harmony rebuilt 1695–97, ~2,377 m², the only building in China with 10 roof beasts; '9,999½ rooms' is folklore — surveys count 8,886 bays across ~980 buildings; built 1406–1420; Jingshan Park sits across the north gate — Palace Museum / UNESCO World Heritage listing + Britannica 'Forbidden City'.
